extraction.name: CT-RATE
extraction.description: A public dataset that pairs 3D medical images (non-contrast 3D chest CT scans) with corresponding textual reports (radiology reports).
extraction.creator: Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Chenyu Wang, Furkan Almas, Ayse Gulnihan Simsek, Sewal Nil Esirgun, Irem Dogan, Omer Faruk Durugol, Benjamin Hou, Suprosanna Shit, Weicheng Dai, Murong Xu, Hadrien Reynaud, Muhammed Furkan Dasdelen, Bastian Wittmann, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Enis Simsar, Mehmet Simsar, Emine Bensu Erdemir, Abdullah Alanbay, Anjany Sekuboyina, Berkan Lafci, Ahmet Kaplan, Zhiyong Lu, Malgorzata Polacin, Bemhard Kainz, Christian Bluethgen, Kayhan Batmanghelich, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, and Bjoem Menze
extraction.publisher: University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, Istanbul Medipol University, Boston University, National Institutes of Health, Imperial College London, ETH Zurich, University Hospital Zurich, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg
extraction.citeAs: Hamamci et al., CT-RATE, CT-CLIP and CT-CHAT, arXiv:2403.17834v4, 2025
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital. It includes non-contrast chest CT volumes acquired between May 2015 and January 2023. The data was anonymized by removing personal information from reports and metadata. Reports were translated from Turkish to English and reviewed by bilingual final-year medical students. CT volumes were filtered to exclude contrast material or body parts other than the chest.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Non-contrast 3D chest CT volumes and corresponding radiology text reports from Istanbul Medipol University Mega Hospital.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: CT volumes were resized to uniform spacing (0.75 mm x/y, 1.5 mm z), center-cropped or padded to 480x480x240 resolution, and converted to Hounsfield Unit values clipped to -1000 to 1000. Reports were anonymized, translated, and reviewed. Multi-abnormality labels were extracted using a finetuned RadBERT model.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: CT volumes were standardized for spacing and resolution. HU values were clipped and normalized. Reports were anonymized using regular expressions to remove dates and identifiers, translated to English, and reviewed by medical students for residual PII and coherence.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-abnormality labels for 18 distinct abnormalities were extracted from radiology reports using an automated text classifier (finetuned RadBERT). This classifier was finetuned on 1,000 manually annotated reports. Additionally, a visual question-answering dataset of over 2.7 million question-answer pairs was generated using Llama 3.1 7B.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 18 abnormality labels per CT volume/report pair; multiple QA pairs per item for the VQA dataset.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 1,000 reports were manually annotated by the authors. Bilingual final-year medical students reviewed translations. Three board-certified radiologists evaluated model outputs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: RadBERT (finetuned for label extraction), Llama 3.1 7B (for VQA generation), TotalSegmentator (for anatomical segmentation labels).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is open-source and publicly accessible via Hugging Face. Code and models are available on GitHub. No specific versioning or update schedule is mentioned beyond the initial release.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains medical imaging data and reports. However, all personal information (patient names, dates, identifiers) was anonymized before release. Demographic data such as age (18-102 years) and sex (41.6% female, 58.4% male) are included in the metadata.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to address the scarcity of comprehensive 3D medical imaging datasets, enabling the development of generalist foundation models for 3D CT. It supports improved patient care, reduced radiologist workload, and advancements in medical AI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is from a single institution (Istanbul Medipol University), which may introduce biases related to geographic and clinical settings. The data reflects real-world heterogeneity in scanners and protocols but may limit generalizability to other populations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Single-institution origin may limit generalizability. The dataset is limited to chest CT volumes. The quality of generated reports and QA pairs depends on the LLM used. The automated labeler may have errors, though high precision/recall was reported. External validation sets were used, but the primary data is from one source.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Specifically for multi-abnormality detection, case retrieval, report generation, and visual question answering in 3D medical imaging.
